_about: Stories from the Pentamerone (Macmillan, 1911), E. F. Strange's selection from Basile's Neapolitan tales of 1634-36. Strange's note says the version follows John Edward Taylor's translation of 1847. The Gutenberg transcription cuts that sentence, so the translator was confirmed against the 1911 printing at the Internet Archive (b1109153), whose text matches. Added at the coordinator's standing relay (2026-10-02/03: choose public-domain storytellers batches; Adam may veto).
_author: Giambattista Basile; tr. John Edward Taylor; ed. E. F. Strange

_translator_not_in_text.basile-stories-from-the-pentamerone: Taylor (claimed, not checkable in the text): the translator is named in the 1911 printing's prefatory note, not in the Gutenberg text. archive.org b1109153 (Macmillan 1911, ed. E. F. Strange) says in that note that its version follows John Edward Taylor's translation of 1847, and its text matches PG 2198 word for word where compared (the opening of the frame story).
